title: Coherent composition from multiarrow spaces
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories and functor objects as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a quasicategory $Q$ and vertices $x_0,\ldots,x_n$, let $H_Q(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ be the fiber of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,Q)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\{0,\ldots,n\},Q)$ over the constant vertex diagrams $x_0,\ldots,x_n$. For $n\geq1$, restriction to consecutive edges is a trivial Kan fibration $H_Q(x_0,\ldots,x_n)\to\prod_{i=1}^n H_Q(x_{i-1},x_i)$, where trivial Kan fibration means lifting all boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq0$. The face and degeneracy maps give composition, identities, associativity and their coherent homotopies, natural in simplicial functors. Inverse edges with inverse-triangle witnesses therefore induce inverse homotopies on precomposition and postcomposition maps. Here $\partial\Delta^n$ denotes the union of the faces of $\Delta^n$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.8.5, Remark 4.6.8.7 and Construction 4.6.8.9 in Subsection 4.6.8 (01PF), Composition of Morphisms. Restriction to spines is the trivial Kan fibration; its face and degeneracy maps retain identity and associativity compatibilities. Unitality and associativity are Propositions 4.6.8.11 and 4.6.8.12.
